# ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/

## Expand description

The `ucd-util` crate contains a smattering of utility functions that implement
various algorithms specified by Unicode. There is no specific goal for
exhaustiveness. Instead, implementations should be added on an as-needed basis.

A *current* design constraint of this crate is that it should not bring in any
large Unicode tables. For example, to use the various property name and value
canonicalization functions, you’ll need to supply your own table, which can
be generated using `ucd-generate`.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_HANGUL_SYLLABLE.html)- HANGUL_ - SYLLABLE
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all Hangul syllable codepoints.
- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_IDEOGRAPH.html)- IDEOGRAPH
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all ideograph codepoints.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_name.html)- property_ - name
- Find the canonical property name for the given normalized property name.
- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_value.html)- property_ - value
- Find the canonical property value for the given normalized property value.
- [character_](https://docs.rs/fn.character_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given character name in place according to UAX44-LM2.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_full_canonical_decomposition.html)- full_ - canonical_ - decomposition
- Return the full canonical decomposition of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [ideograph_](https://docs.rs/fn.ideograph_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given ideograph codepoint.
- [property_](https://docs.rs/fn.property_values.html)- values
- Find the set of possible property values for a given property.
- [symbolic_](https://docs.rs/fn.symbolic_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given symbolic name in place according to UAX44-LM3.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyTable.html)- Table
- The type of a property name table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValueTable.html)- Value - Table
- Type of a property value table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html)- Values
- A mapping of property values for a specific property.

# ucd-util 0.2.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest

# ucd-util

A library for small auxiliary Unicode functions. This includes things like symbol or character name canonicalization, ideograph name generation and helper functions for searching property name and value tables.

### Documentation

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# rsclaw-channel 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rsclaw-channel/0.1.0

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/rsclaw-channel/0.1.0/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

Channel subsystem.

TODO: Channel instances are stored behind `OnceCell` (set once at startup).
This prevents hot-adding or replacing channels at runtime. Migrate to
`ArcSwap` to support the channel hot-add feature (see feature backlog).

A *channel* is an integration point where messages arrive (Telegram,
Discord, CLI, etc.). Each channel implementation:

- Receives inbound messages and forwards them to the gateway router.
- Sends outbound replies (with optional chunking / preview streaming).
- Enforces `dmPolicy`(pairing / allowlist / open / disabled).

Modules:

- `mod`—- `Channel`trait,- `DmPolicyEnforcer`,- `PairingStore`
- `chunker`— text chunking with code-fence protection
- `telegram`— Telegram Bot API client
- `discord`— Discord Bot WebSocket + REST
- `slack`— Slack Socket Mode + Web API
- `whatsapp`— WhatsApp Cloud API (webhook)
- `signal`— Signal via signal-cli JSON-RPC
- `dingtalk`— DingTalk Robot Stream Mode + REST
- `line`— LINE Messaging API (webhook)
- `zalo`— Zalo Official Account API (webhook)
- `matrix`— Matrix Client-Server API (long-poll sync)
- `cli`— CLI interactive channel

---

# rustledger_lsp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-lsp/0.19.1/rustledger_lsp/

## Expand description

Language Server Protocol implementation for Beancount.

This crate provides an LSP server for Beancount files, enabling IDE features like:

- Real-time syntax error diagnostics
- Autocompletion for accounts, currencies, payees
- Go-to-definition for accounts
- Hover information
- Document symbols (outline view)

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

The server follows rust-analyzer’s architecture:

- **Main loop**: Handles LSP messages, applies changes, dispatches requests
- **Query database**: Salsa-inspired incremental computation
- **Handlers**: Process LSP requests against immutable snapshots

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use ledger_state::`- [LedgerState](https://docs.rs/ledger_state/struct.LedgerState.html);
- `pub use ledger_state::`- [LspConfig](https://docs.rs/ledger_state/struct.LspConfig.html);
- `pub use main_loop::`- [run_main_loop](https://docs.rs/main_loop/fn.run_main_loop.html);
- `pub use main_loop::`- [run_main_loop_with_exit_action](https://docs.rs/main_loop/fn.run_main_loop_with_exit_action.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [handlers](https://docs.rs/handlers/index.html)
- LSP request and notification handlers.
- [ledger_](https://docs.rs/ledger_state/index.html)- state
- Ledger state management for multi-file support.
- [main_](https://docs.rs/main_loop/index.html)- loop
- Main event loop for the LSP server.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Server](https://docs.rs/struct.Server.html)
- The LSP server.
- [Snapshot](https://docs.rs/struct.Snapshot.html)
- An immutable snapshot of the world state.
- [Vfs](https://docs.rs/struct.Vfs.html)
- Virtual file system for managing open documents.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [VERSION](https://docs.rs/constant.VERSION.html)
- LSP server version.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [start_](https://docs.rs/fn.start_stdio.html)- stdio
- Start the LSP server using stdio transport.

# lexir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lexir/0.2.0/lexir/

## Expand description

`lexir`: lexical IR built on `postings`.

Lexical retrieval built on `postings`:

- `postings`provides postings lists + candidate planning (no false negatives).
- `lexir`provides- **scoring + ranking**(BM25 / TF-IDF) over- `postings`.

Scope:

- In-memory indexes
- Deterministic ranking (tie-break by doc id)
- Caller-provided token streams (so different products can choose tokenization)

Non-goals:

- Storing document content (index-only)
- Phrase queries / positional postings
- Query language beyond “bag of terms”

References:

- Robertson & Walker (1994): probabilistic retrieval foundations
- Robertson & Zaragoza (2009): BM25 and beyond
- Spärck Jones (1972): term specificity / IDF motivation

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [bm25](https://docs.rs/bm25/index.html)
- Okapi BM25 over `postings::PostingsIndex`.
- [query_](https://docs.rs/query_likelihood/index.html)- likelihood
- Query likelihood language model retrieval.
- [tfidf](https://docs.rs/tfidf/index.html)
- TF-IDF scoring over the shared postings-backed index.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors for lexical retrieval.

---

# rustledger_ffi_wasi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-ffi-wasi/0.19.1/rustledger_ffi_wasi/

## Expand description

Slimmed FFI-support helpers for the rustledger WASI component FFI.

[§](https://docs.rs#phase-5-1419-is-complete)Phase 5 (#1419) is complete

This crate used to expose a wasip1 JSON-RPC 2.0 embedding API (a server
binary in `main.rs` + a `jsonrpc` router) plus a `Directive → JSON` output
DTO. Both are gone: the JSON-RPC surface was retired earlier in Phase 5
([#1419](https://github.com/rustledger/rustledger/issues/1419)) now that the
typed WASI Preview 2 / Component Model binding,
[ rustledger-ffi-component](https://github.com/rustledger/rustledger/issues/1384)
(#1384), is the default embedding path (default in rustfava as of Phase 4);
the output DTO was removed once the component switched to converting
core→WIT directly.

What remains is a **library only** of FFI-support glue the component reuses:
the loader orchestration ([ helpers](https://docs.rs/helpers/index.html)), the WIT-input construction path
(

[+ the](https://docs.rs/fn.input_entry_to_directive.html)

`input_entry_to_directive``Input*` types) and directive hashing
([). These survivors are deliberately FFI glue kept OUT of the core](https://docs.rs/hash/fn.compute_directive_hash.html)

`compute_directive_hash``rustledger-loader` crate, so the crate is retained slimmed
rather than relocated or deleted (the “retained … document the decision”
outcome of #1419 item 6).## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use hash::`- [compute_directive_hash](https://docs.rs/hash/fn.compute_directive_hash.html);

- Input amount for entry creation.

# rustledger - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger/0.19.1/rustledger/

## Expand description

Beancount CLI tools.

This crate provides command-line tools for working with Beancount files:

- `rledger check`/- `bean-check`: Validate a beancount file
- `rledger format`/- `bean-format`: Format a beancount file
- `rledger query`/- `bean-query`: Query with BQL
- `rledger report`/- `bean-report`: Generate reports
- `rledger doctor`/- `bean-doctor`: Debugging tools

[§](https://docs.rs#example-usage)Example Usage

```
rledger check ledger.beancount
rledger format ledger.beancount
rledger query ledger.beancount "SELECT account, SUM(position)"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#related-crates)Related Crates

rustledger is a workspace with several crates:

| Crate | Description |
|---|---|
| `rustledger-core` | Core types (Amount, Position, Inventory, Directives) |
| `rustledger-parser` | Lexer and parser with error recovery |
| `rustledger-loader` | File loading, includes, options |
| `rustledger-booking` | Interpolation and booking engine |
| `rustledger-validate` | Validation with error reporting |
| `rustledger-query` | BQL query engine |
| `rustledger-plugin` | Native and WASM plugin system |
| `rustledger-wasm` | WebAssembly library target |
| `rustledger-importer` | Import framework for bank statements |
| `rustledger-lsp` | Language Server Protocol implementation |
| `rustledger-ffi-wasi` | FFI via WASI for embedding |

# rustledger_wasm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-wasm/0.19.1/rustledger_wasm/

## Expand description

Beancount WASM Bindings.

This crate provides WebAssembly bindings for using Beancount from JavaScript/TypeScript.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Parse Beancount files (single and multi-file with includes)
- Validate ledgers
- Run BQL queries
- Format directives
- `ParsedLedger`
- `Ledger`

[§](https://docs.rs#example-javascript)Example (JavaScript)

```
import init, { parse, validateSource, query } from '@rustledger/wasm';
await init();
const source = `
2024-01-01 open Assets:Bank USD
2024-01-15 * "Coffee"
  Expenses:Food  5.00 USD
  Assets:Bank   -5.00 USD
`;
const result = parse(source);
if (result.errors.length === 0) {
    const validation = validateSource(source);
    console.log('Validation errors:', validation.errors);
}
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Conversion functions between Beancount types and JSON DTOs.

- Data transfer objects for WASM serialization.

- A parsed and validated single-file ledger with editor features.

# rustledger_completion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-completion/0.19.1/rustledger_completion/

## Expand description

Editor-agnostic completion logic for Beancount sources.

This crate is the single source of truth for the completion logic
shared between the LSP (`rustledger-lsp`) and the WASM editor
(`rustledger-wasm`). It is deliberately pure: no clock access, no
`lsp-types`, no `wasm-bindgen`. Callers supply the live data
(account/currency/payee/tag/link string lists and “today’s” date)
and map the neutral [ CompletionCandidate](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletionCandidate.html) results into their own
editor-specific item types.

The two responsibilities are:

- **Context detection**—- `offset_to_byte`- `PositionEncoding`- `classify_context`- `CompletionContext`
- **Candidate generation**— the- `*_candidates`functions produce neutral- `CompletionCandidate`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Completion](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletionCandidate.html)- Candidate
- A neutral, editor-agnostic completion candidate.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Completion](https://docs.rs/enum.CompletionContext.html)- Context
- Completion context detected from cursor position.
- [Completion](https://docs.rs/enum.CompletionKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of a completion candidate.
- [Position](https://docs.rs/enum.PositionEncoding.html)- Encoding
- How a position offset is encoded by the caller.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ACCOUNT_](https://docs.rs/constant.ACCOUNT_TYPES.html)- TYPES
- Standard Beancount account types.
- [DIRECTIVES](https://docs.rs/constant.DIRECTIVES.html)
- Standard Beancount directives.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [account_](https://docs.rs/fn.account_segment_candidates.html)- segment_ - candidates
- Candidates for the next account segment after a `prefix`.
- [account_](https://docs.rs/fn.account_start_candidates.html)- start_ - candidates
- Candidates when starting an account name: the standard account types followed by every known account.
- [after_](https://docs.rs/fn.after_date_candidates.html)- date_ - candidates
- Candidates after a date: the directive keywords.
- [classify_](https://docs.rs/fn.classify_context.html)- context
- Classify the completion context from the text before the cursor.
- [currency_](https://docs.rs/fn.currency_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a currency after an amount.
- [line_](https://docs.rs/fn.line_start_candidates.html)- start_ - candidates
- Candidates at line start: a single date template using the supplied
`today`string (the crate is clock-free; each adapter passes its own date).
- [link_](https://docs.rs/fn.link_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a link after `^`(issue #1268). Mirrors`tag_candidates``label`and dropped in`insert_text`.
- [offset_](https://docs.rs/fn.offset_to_byte.html)- to_ - byte
- Map a position `offset`(in the given`encoding`) into a byte offset into`line`, clamped to a char boundary.
- [payee_](https://docs.rs/fn.payee_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a payee/narration inside a string. Returns all known
payees — the client filters (issue #1183, the `.take(20)`trap).
- [tag_](https://docs.rs/fn.tag_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a tag after `#`(issue #1268).

# rustledger_importer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-importer/0.19.1/rustledger_importer/

## Expand description

Import framework for rustledger

This crate provides the infrastructure for extracting transactions from bank statements, credit card statements, and other financial documents.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The import system is modeled after Python beancount’s bean-extract. It uses
a trait-based approach where each importer implements the [ Importer](https://docs.rs/trait.Importer.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use rustledger_importer::{ImporterConfig, ImporterRegistry};
use std::path::Path;
// Build the per-call config (CSV in this example).
let config = ImporterConfig::csv()
    .account("Assets:Bank:Checking")
    .date_column("Date")
    .narration_column("Description")
    .amount_column("Amount")
    .build()
    .unwrap();
// Dispatch through the registry — picks OfxImporter for .ofx/.qfx,
// CsvImporter for .csv. Returns an error for unknown extensions.
let registry = ImporterRegistry::with_builtins();
// let result = registry.extract(Path::new("bank.csv"), &config)?;
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [ImporterConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.ImporterConfig.html);
- `pub use ofx_importer::`- [OfxImporter](https://docs.rs/ofx_importer/struct.OfxImporter.html);
- `pub use registry::`- [ImporterRegistry](https://docs.rs/registry/struct.ImporterRegistry.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Configuration for importers.
- [csv_](https://docs.rs/csv_importer/index.html)- importer
- CSV file importer.
- [csv_](https://docs.rs/csv_inference/index.html)- inference
- CSV format auto-inference.
- [ofx_](https://docs.rs/ofx_importer/index.html)- importer
- OFX/QFX file importer.
- [registry](https://docs.rs/registry/index.html)
- Registry for importers.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Enriched](https://docs.rs/struct.EnrichedImportResult.html)- Import - Result

# rustledger_query - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-query/0.19.1/rustledger_query/

## Expand description

Beancount Query Language (BQL) engine.

This crate provides a SQL-like query language for analyzing Beancount ledger data.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

BQL is a specialized query language designed for financial data analysis. It operates on transaction postings while respecting double-entry bookkeeping constraints.

[§](https://docs.rs#query-types)Query Types

- `SELECT`- General purpose queries with filtering, grouping, and ordering
- `JOURNAL`- Shorthand for account statements
- `BALANCES`- Shorthand for account balance tables
- `PRINT`- Output filtered transactions in Beancount syntax

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use rustledger_query::parse;
let query = parse("SELECT account, SUM(position) WHERE account ~ \"Expenses:\" GROUP BY account").unwrap();
println!("{:?}", query);
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [ParseError](https://docs.rs/error/struct.ParseError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [QueryError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.QueryError.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [Executor](https://docs.rs/executor/struct.Executor.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [Interval](https://docs.rs/executor/struct.Interval.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [IntervalUnit](https://docs.rs/executor/enum.IntervalUnit.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [QueryResult](https://docs.rs/executor/struct.QueryResult.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [Value](https://docs.rs/executor/enum.Value.html);
- `pub use parser::`- [parse](https://docs.rs/parser/fn.parse.html);
- `pub use price::`- [PriceDatabase](https://docs.rs/price/struct.PriceDatabase.html);

# rustledger_plugin - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-plugin/0.19.1/rustledger_plugin/

## Expand description

Beancount WASM Plugin Runtime.

This crate provides a plugin system for extending Beancount’s functionality. Plugins can be written in any language that compiles to WebAssembly, or as native Rust code for maximum performance.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

The plugin system uses wasmtime as the WASM runtime with `MessagePack`
serialization for passing data across the WASM boundary.

[§](https://docs.rs#plugin-types)Plugin Types

- **WASM Plugins**: Sandboxed plugins loaded from- `.wasm`files
- **Native Plugins**: Built-in plugins implemented in Rust

[§](https://docs.rs#built-in-plugins-31)Built-in Plugins (31)

See the [plugin reference](https://rustledger.github.io/docs/reference/plugins) for the full list.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use rustledger_plugin::{PluginManager, PluginInput, PluginOptions};
let mut manager = PluginManager::new();
manager.load(Path::new("my_plugin.wasm"))?;
let input = PluginInput {
    directives: vec![],
    options: PluginOptions::default(),
    config: None,
};
let output = manager.execute_all(input)?;
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# rustledger_loader - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-loader/0.19.1/rustledger_loader/

## Expand description

Beancount file loader with include resolution.

This crate handles loading beancount files, resolving includes, and collecting options. It builds on the parser to provide a complete loading pipeline.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Recursive include resolution with cycle detection
- Options collection and parsing
- Plugin directive collection
- Source map for error reporting
- Push/pop tag and metadata handling
- Automatic GPG decryption for encrypted files (`.gpg`,`.asc`)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

# postings - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/postings/0.2.0/postings/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#postings)postings

A small inverted-index core built around postings lists.

[§](https://docs.rs#scope-deliberate)Scope (deliberate)

- This crate is **index-only**: it does not store document content.
- It supports **candidate generation**with**no false negatives**(a caller may choose to verify candidates with an exact matcher).
- It uses a Lucene-style mental model: immutable “segments” (here: append-only batches) and logical deletes.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-modules)Optional modules

- `postings::codec`: low-level codecs (varint/gap) for postings payloads (in this repo).
- `postings::positional`(feature- `positional`): positional postings for phrase/proximity evaluation.
- `postings::raw`(feature- `raw-segment`): byte- and file-backed raw segment reader experiments.

[§](https://docs.rs#non-goals-for-now)Non-goals (for now)

- Full on-disk compaction
- Rich query language beyond candidate generation and sparse top-k scoring

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [codec](https://docs.rs/codec/index.html)
- Low-level codecs and iterator contracts for postings payloads.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Planner](https://docs.rs/struct.PlannerConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for candidate planning / bailout.
- [Postings](https://docs.rs/struct.PostingsIndex.html)- Index
- A postings-based inverted index with segment-style updates.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Candidate](https://docs.rs/enum.CandidatePlan.html)- Plan
- Planner output for candidate generation.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors returned by `postings`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Weight](https://docs.rs/trait.Weight.html)
- Trait for term weight types in posting lists.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [DocId](https://docs.rs/type.DocId.html)
- Document identifier.

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/0.2.2

# ucd-util

A library for small auxiliary Unicode functions. This includes things like symbol or character name canonicalization, ideograph name generation and helper functions for searching property name and value tables.

# ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/0.2.2/target-redirect/ucd_util/

## Expand description

The `ucd-util` crate contains a smattering of utility functions that implement
various algorithms specified by Unicode. There is no specific goal for
exhaustiveness. Instead, implementations should be added on an as-needed basis.

A *current* design constraint of this crate is that it should not bring in any
large Unicode tables. For example, to use the various property name and value
canonicalization functions, you’ll need to supply your own table, which can
be generated using `ucd-generate`.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_HANGUL_SYLLABLE.html)- HANGUL_ - SYLLABLE
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all Hangul syllable codepoints.
- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_IDEOGRAPH.html)- IDEOGRAPH
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all ideograph codepoints.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_name.html)- property_ - name
- Find the canonical property name for the given normalized property name.
- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_value.html)- property_ - value
- Find the canonical property value for the given normalized property value.
- [character_](https://docs.rs/fn.character_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given character name in place according to UAX44-LM2.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_full_canonical_decomposition.html)- full_ - canonical_ - decomposition
- Return the full canonical decomposition of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [ideograph_](https://docs.rs/fn.ideograph_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given ideograph codepoint.
- [property_](https://docs.rs/fn.property_values.html)- values
- Find the set of possible property values for a given property.
- [symbolic_](https://docs.rs/fn.symbolic_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given symbolic name in place according to UAX44-LM3.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyTable.html)- Table
- The type of a property name table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValueTable.html)- Value - Table
- Type of a property value table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html)- Values
- A mapping of property values for a specific property.

---

# canonical_property_name in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.canonical_property_name.html

```
pub fn canonical_property_name(
    property_table:
```
[PropertyTable](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyTable.html),
    normalized_property_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>## Expand description

Find the canonical property name for the given normalized property name.

If no such property exists, then `None` is returned.

The normalized property name must have been normalized according to
UAX44 LM3, which can be done using `symbolic_name_normalize`.

---

# canonical_property_value in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.canonical_property_value.html

```
pub fn canonical_property_value(
    property_values:
```
[PropertyValues](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html),
    normalized_property_value: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>## Expand description

Find the canonical property value for the given normalized property value.

The given property values should correspond to the values for the property
under question, which can be found using `property_values`.

If no such property value exists, then `None` is returned.

The normalized property value must have been normalized according to
UAX44 LM3, which can be done using `symbolic_name_normalize`.

---

# character_name_normalize in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.character_name_normalize.html

`pub fn character_name_normalize(string: &mut `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))## Expand description

Normalize the given character name in place according to UAX44-LM2.

See: https://unicode.org/reports/tr44/#UAX44-LM2

---

# hangul_full_canonical_decomposition in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.hangul_full_canonical_decomposition.html

## Expand description

Return the full canonical decomposition of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.

If the decomposition does not have any trailing consonant, then the third
part of the tuple returned is `None`.

If the given codepoint does not correspond to a precomposed Hangul
codepoint in the inclusive range `AC00..D7A3`, then this returns `None`.

This implements the algorithms described in Unicode 3.12 and Unicode 4.8.

---

# hangul_name in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.hangul_name.html

## Expand description

Return the character name of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.

If the given codepoint does not correspond to a precomposed Hangul
codepoint in the inclusive range `AC00..D7A3`, then this returns `None`.

This implements the algorithms described in Unicode 3.12 and Unicode 4.8.

The `table` given should be a map from codepoint to the corresponding
Jamo short name for that codepoint. If you’re using `ucd-generate`, then
the table can be generated via the `jamo-short-name` sub-command.

---

# ideograph_name in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.ideograph_name.html

## Expand description

Return the character name of the given ideograph codepoint.

This operation is only defined on ideographic codepoints. This includes precisely the following inclusive ranges:

- `3400..4DB5`
- `4E00..9FD5`
- `20000..2A6D6`
- `2A700..2B734`
- `2B740..2B81D`
- `2B820..2CEA1`
- `17000..187EC`
- `F900..FA6D`
- `FA70..FAD9`
- `2F800..2FA1D`

If the given codepoint is not in any of the above ranges, then `None` is
returned.

This implements the algorithm described in Unicode 4.8.

---

# property_values in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.property_values.html

```
pub fn property_values(
    property_value_table:
```
[PropertyValueTable](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValueTable.html),
    canonical_property_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[PropertyValues](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html)>## Expand description

Find the set of possible property values for a given property.

The set returned is a mapping expressed as a sorted list of tuples. The first element of each tuple is a normalized property value while the second element of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property value.

If no such property exists, then `None` is returned.

The given property name must be in its canonical form, which can be
found using `canonical_property_name`.

---

# symbolic_name_normalize in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/fn.symbolic_name_normalize.html

`pub fn symbolic_name_normalize(string: &mut `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))## Expand description

Normalize the given symbolic name in place according to UAX44-LM3.

A “symbolic name” typically corresponds to property names and property value aliases. Note, though, that it should not be applied to property string values.

See: https://unicode.org/reports/tr44/#UAX44-LM2

---

# PropertyTable in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/type.PropertyTable.html

## Expand description

The type of a property name table.

A property name table is a sequence of sorted tuples, where the first value in each tuple is a normalized property name and the second value of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property name.

---

# PropertyValueTable in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/type.PropertyValueTable.html

`pub type PropertyValueTable = &'static [(&'static `[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), [PropertyValues](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html))];## Expand description

Type of a property value table.

A property value table maps property names to a mapping of property values, where the mapping of property values is represented by a sequence of tuples. The first element of each tuple is a normalized property value while the second element of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property value.

Note that a property value table only includes values for properties that are catalogs, enumerations or binary properties. Properties that have string values (such as case or decomposition mappings), numeric values or are miscellaneous are not represented in this table.

---

# PropertyValues in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/0.2.2/ucd_util/type.PropertyValues.html

## Expand description

A mapping of property values for a specific property.

The first element of each tuple is a normalized property value while the second element of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property value.

---

# ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util/latest/ucd_util/

## Expand description

The `ucd-util` crate contains a smattering of utility functions that implement
various algorithms specified by Unicode. There is no specific goal for
exhaustiveness. Instead, implementations should be added on an as-needed basis.

A *current* design constraint of this crate is that it should not bring in any
large Unicode tables. For example, to use the various property name and value
canonicalization functions, you’ll need to supply your own table, which can
be generated using `ucd-generate`.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_HANGUL_SYLLABLE.html)- HANGUL_ - SYLLABLE
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all Hangul syllable codepoints.
- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_IDEOGRAPH.html)- IDEOGRAPH
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all ideograph codepoints.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_name.html)- property_ - name
- Find the canonical property name for the given normalized property name.
- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_value.html)- property_ - value
- Find the canonical property value for the given normalized property value.
- [character_](https://docs.rs/fn.character_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given character name in place according to UAX44-LM2.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_full_canonical_decomposition.html)- full_ - canonical_ - decomposition
- Return the full canonical decomposition of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [ideograph_](https://docs.rs/fn.ideograph_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given ideograph codepoint.
- [property_](https://docs.rs/fn.property_values.html)- values
- Find the set of possible property values for a given property.
- [symbolic_](https://docs.rs/fn.symbolic_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given symbolic name in place according to UAX44-LM3.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyTable.html)- Table
- The type of a property name table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValueTable.html)- Value - Table
- Type of a property value table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html)- Values
- A mapping of property values for a specific property.

# ucd-util 0.2.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ucd-util

## Expand description

The `ucd-util` crate contains a smattering of utility functions that implement
various algorithms specified by Unicode. There is no specific goal for
exhaustiveness. Instead, implementations should be added on an as-needed basis.

A *current* design constraint of this crate is that it should not bring in any
large Unicode tables. For example, to use the various property name and value
canonicalization functions, you’ll need to supply your own table, which can
be generated using `ucd-generate`.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_HANGUL_SYLLABLE.html)- HANGUL_ - SYLLABLE
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all Hangul syllable codepoints.
- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_IDEOGRAPH.html)- IDEOGRAPH
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all ideograph codepoints.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_name.html)- property_ - name
- Find the canonical property name for the given normalized property name.
- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_value.html)- property_ - value
- Find the canonical property value for the given normalized property value.
- [character_](https://docs.rs/fn.character_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given character name in place according to UAX44-LM2.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_full_canonical_decomposition.html)- full_ - canonical_ - decomposition
- Return the full canonical decomposition of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [ideograph_](https://docs.rs/fn.ideograph_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given ideograph codepoint.
- [property_](https://docs.rs/fn.property_values.html)- values
- Find the set of possible property values for a given property.
- [symbolic_](https://docs.rs/fn.symbolic_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given symbolic name in place according to UAX44-LM3.

# ucd-util 0.2.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/source/README.md

```
ucd-util
========
A library for small auxiliary Unicode functions. This includes things like
symbol or character name canonicalization, ideograph name generation and helper
functions for searching property name and value tables.
[![Build status](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ucd-generate/workflows/ci/badge.svg)](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ucd-generate/actions)
[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/ucd-util.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/ucd-util)
https://docs.rs/ucd-util
This project is licensed under either of
 *  *
The data in [`src/unicode_tables/`](src/unicode_tables) is licensed inder the Unicode License
Agreement ([LICENSE-UNICODE](LICENSE-UNICODE) or
https://www.unicode.org/copyright.html#License).
```

# ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/index.html

## Expand description

The `ucd-util` crate contains a smattering of utility functions that implement
various algorithms specified by Unicode. There is no specific goal for
exhaustiveness. Instead, implementations should be added on an as-needed basis.

A *current* design constraint of this crate is that it should not bring in any
large Unicode tables. For example, to use the various property name and value
canonicalization functions, you’ll need to supply your own table, which can
be generated using `ucd-generate`.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_HANGUL_SYLLABLE.html)- HANGUL_ - SYLLABLE
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all Hangul syllable codepoints.
- [RANGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.RANGE_IDEOGRAPH.html)- IDEOGRAPH
- A set of ranges that corresponds to the set of all ideograph codepoints.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_name.html)- property_ - name
- Find the canonical property name for the given normalized property name.
- [canonical_](https://docs.rs/fn.canonical_property_value.html)- property_ - value
- Find the canonical property value for the given normalized property value.
- [character_](https://docs.rs/fn.character_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given character name in place according to UAX44-LM2.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_full_canonical_decomposition.html)- full_ - canonical_ - decomposition
- Return the full canonical decomposition of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [hangul_](https://docs.rs/fn.hangul_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.
- [ideograph_](https://docs.rs/fn.ideograph_name.html)- name
- Return the character name of the given ideograph codepoint.
- [property_](https://docs.rs/fn.property_values.html)- values
- Find the set of possible property values for a given property.
- [symbolic_](https://docs.rs/fn.symbolic_name_normalize.html)- name_ - normalize
- Normalize the given symbolic name in place according to UAX44-LM3.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyTable.html)- Table
- The type of a property name table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValueTable.html)- Value - Table
- Type of a property value table.
- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html)- Values
- A mapping of property values for a specific property.

---

# canonical_property_name in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.canonical_property_name.html

```
pub fn canonical_property_name(
    property_table:
```
[PropertyTable](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyTable.html),
    normalized_property_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>## Expand description

Find the canonical property name for the given normalized property name.

If no such property exists, then `None` is returned.

The normalized property name must have been normalized according to
UAX44 LM3, which can be done using `symbolic_name_normalize`.

---

# canonical_property_value in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.canonical_property_value.html

```
pub fn canonical_property_value(
    property_values:
```
[PropertyValues](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html),
    normalized_property_value: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>## Expand description

Find the canonical property value for the given normalized property value.

The given property values should correspond to the values for the property
under question, which can be found using `property_values`.

If no such property value exists, then `None` is returned.

The normalized property value must have been normalized according to
UAX44 LM3, which can be done using `symbolic_name_normalize`.

---

# character_name_normalize in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.character_name_normalize.html

`pub fn character_name_normalize(string: &mut `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))## Expand description

Normalize the given character name in place according to UAX44-LM2.

See: https://unicode.org/reports/tr44/#UAX44-LM2

---

# hangul_full_canonical_decomposition in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.hangul_full_canonical_decomposition.html

## Expand description

Return the full canonical decomposition of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.

If the decomposition does not have any trailing consonant, then the third
part of the tuple returned is `None`.

If the given codepoint does not correspond to a precomposed Hangul
codepoint in the inclusive range `AC00..D7A3`, then this returns `None`.

This implements the algorithms described in Unicode 3.12 and Unicode 4.8.

---

# hangul_name in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.hangul_name.html

## Expand description

Return the character name of the given precomposed Hangul codepoint.

If the given codepoint does not correspond to a precomposed Hangul
codepoint in the inclusive range `AC00..D7A3`, then this returns `None`.

This implements the algorithms described in Unicode 3.12 and Unicode 4.8.

The `table` given should be a map from codepoint to the corresponding
Jamo short name for that codepoint. If you’re using `ucd-generate`, then
the table can be generated via the `jamo-short-name` sub-command.

---

# ideograph_name in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.ideograph_name.html

## Expand description

Return the character name of the given ideograph codepoint.

This operation is only defined on ideographic codepoints. This includes precisely the following inclusive ranges:

- `3400..4DB5`
- `4E00..9FD5`
- `20000..2A6D6`
- `2A700..2B734`
- `2B740..2B81D`
- `2B820..2CEA1`
- `17000..187EC`
- `F900..FA6D`
- `FA70..FAD9`
- `2F800..2FA1D`

If the given codepoint is not in any of the above ranges, then `None` is
returned.

This implements the algorithm described in Unicode 4.8.

---

# property_values in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.property_values.html

```
pub fn property_values(
    property_value_table:
```
[PropertyValueTable](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValueTable.html),
    canonical_property_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[PropertyValues](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html)>## Expand description

Find the set of possible property values for a given property.

The set returned is a mapping expressed as a sorted list of tuples. The first element of each tuple is a normalized property value while the second element of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property value.

If no such property exists, then `None` is returned.

The given property name must be in its canonical form, which can be
found using `canonical_property_name`.

---

# symbolic_name_normalize in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/fn.symbolic_name_normalize.html

`pub fn symbolic_name_normalize(string: &mut `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))## Expand description

Normalize the given symbolic name in place according to UAX44-LM3.

A “symbolic name” typically corresponds to property names and property value aliases. Note, though, that it should not be applied to property string values.

See: https://unicode.org/reports/tr44/#UAX44-LM2

---

# PropertyTable in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/type.PropertyTable.html

## Expand description

The type of a property name table.

A property name table is a sequence of sorted tuples, where the first value in each tuple is a normalized property name and the second value of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property name.

---

# PropertyValueTable in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/type.PropertyValueTable.html

`pub type PropertyValueTable = &'static [(&'static `[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), [PropertyValues](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyValues.html))];## Expand description

Type of a property value table.

A property value table maps property names to a mapping of property values, where the mapping of property values is represented by a sequence of tuples. The first element of each tuple is a normalized property value while the second element of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property value.

Note that a property value table only includes values for properties that are catalogs, enumerations or binary properties. Properties that have string values (such as case or decomposition mappings), numeric values or are miscellaneous are not represented in this table.

---

# PropertyValues in ucd_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ucd-util/latest/target-redirect/ucd_util/type.PropertyValues.html

## Expand description

A mapping of property values for a specific property.

The first element of each tuple is a normalized property value while the second element of each tuple is the corresponding canonical property value.

---

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

# clap - Rust

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

}

    for _ in 0..args.count {

```

```
$ demo --help

Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
